content:
Search engine optimization, often called SEO, helps search engines understand your website and helps people decide whether to visit it. For your church's site, begin with clear information a guest can use.

Search Console can show how your site appears in Google Search. Website analytics can help you understand activity after someone arrives. Use these reports to ask specific questions about the site.

---

## Choose the question before the tool

Start with the question you need to answer. Google's tools serve different purposes.

| Your question | Where to start |
|---|---|
| Can Google find an important page? | Search Console's URL Inspection tool |
| Which searches bring people to the site? | Search Console's Performance report |
| Where does website traffic come from? | Google Analytics' Traffic acquisition report |
| Is a website action being recorded? | Analytics' Realtime report or DebugView |

Search Console is free. You do not have to register for it to appear in Google Search, and registration does not buy a better position.

<Callout type="important">
Google documentation checked October 16, 2026. Before setup, confirm current instructions and policies with Google Search Central, Search Console Help, and Google Analytics Help. Report names and available settings can change.
</Callout>

---

## Connect Search Console to your site

Open Search Console and check whether an existing owner can grant you access. Otherwise, add a website property and complete ownership verification.

Choose the property type that fits the access you have:

- A Domain property covers its subdomains and protocols. For an ordinary independently hosted domain, verification uses a DNS record.
- A URL-prefix property covers addresses beginning with the exact prefix you enter, including the protocol. Google offers several verification methods for this type.

For example, `https://www.example.org/` does not include `https://example.org/`. Ask the person managing your domain or website to help with verification if needed. Check the selected property before interpreting an empty report.

---

## Check whether important pages are indexed

Indexing means Google has processed a page and added it to its index, making it eligible to appear in results. Use URL Inspection to check your home page and other important public pages individually.

If a page is missing, read the reported reason with your website provider. Some pages legitimately remain unindexed, including duplicates. Avoid treating every unindexed address as an error.

You can consider submitting a sitemap, a file listing the pages you want search engines to know about. Google can discover pages without one, and your website platform may already provide it. Ask your provider before creating a second process.

<Callout type="tip">
Being indexed makes a page eligible for search results. It does not guarantee that your page will appear for a particular search or hold a fixed ranking.
</Callout>

---

## Make each page clear and useful

Write for the person trying to understand your church. Use ordinary language, readable paragraphs, and headings that describe the content. Keep information current and connect relevant pages with descriptive links.

Give each page a distinct, concise title that matches its contents. As an example, a visit page could use "Plan a visit | Grace Church" instead of repeating "Home" across the site. Use your real church name in the example's place.

Write a page-specific meta description, the summary field your website editor may provide. Google often creates its search description from the page itself and may use your meta description when it fits better. The wording you enter is a suggestion, rather than a promise about the result shown.

Avoid repeating city names or church-related phrases merely to fill the page. Google's guidance rejects keyword stuffing and does not prescribe a magic word count for ranking.

---

## Add Analytics if you need website activity reports

Google Analytics 4, commonly called GA4, measures website and app activity using events. If you choose it, follow Google's setup guide with your website provider.

- [ ] Create or select the Analytics account and property.
- [ ] Check the reporting time zone.
- [ ] Add a Web data stream for the church website.
- [ ] Review the enhanced measurement options and the events you intend to collect.
- [ ] Follow your platform's supported Google tag installation instructions.

Some website builders provide a field for the Google tag ID. Others need a different installation method. Ask your provider which route your site uses.

Check the installation using Realtime. If data is missing, confirm the account, property, tag ID, and page installation before drawing conclusions about traffic. Google warns that installing both the direct Google tag and Tag Manager implementations can overcount activity.

---

## Read the labels before comparing numbers

In Search Console, impressions count appearances in search results; clicks count clicks to your site from those results. Click-through rate divides clicks by impressions. Use the Queries and Pages views to see what the totals describe, and record the date range when comparing reports.

In Analytics, Traffic acquisition reports where new and returning users' sessions come from. Its channel groups include Organic Search, Direct, and Email. If that report is missing from your navigation, an Editor or Administrator can add it back.

A session is a period of interaction with your site. A person can start multiple sessions, and Analytics estimates session counts. Keep the label "sessions" when sharing that number.

An event records an interaction or occurrence, such as loading a page or clicking a link. You can mark an important measured action as a key event. Confirm the event and its parameters in Realtime or DebugView before relying on it.

---

## Keep personal information out of measurement

Google prohibits sending information it can recognize as personally identifiable, including email addresses and personal mobile numbers, to Analytics. Its basic page tag collects page addresses and titles, so check those as well as form fields and event settings.

Ask your provider to inspect URL parameters, search terms, and custom event data for personal information.

Google requires disclosure of Analytics use and how it collects and processes data. Review the site's privacy notice against the actual setup before enabling it. Review account data-sharing choices, too.

<Callout type="warning">
Do not send names, email addresses, or personal form responses as Analytics event details. Check the data being sent, rather than assuming a generic event name makes its contents safe.
</Callout>

---

## Review the site without watching it all day

Google suggests checking Search Console around monthly or after site content changes. It also sends email alerts when it finds new issues.

Use this checklist for a focused review:

- [ ] Check for reported search problems affecting important public pages.
- [ ] Review search queries and pages over the selected period.
- [ ] Recheck titles and descriptions when page content changes.
- [ ] If Analytics is installed, check traffic sources and verify the actions you measure.
- [ ] Review what information the measurement tools receive.

<Callout type="scripture">
*"He who responds with a word before he hears, It is folly and shame to him."* — Proverbs 18:13 (LSB)
</Callout>

title: Website Analytics and Search Basics

sources.claim: Opening and content section: SEO helps search engines understand content and readers decide whether to visit; write useful current content with descriptive links; avoid stuffing and ranking word-count targets. Church examples apply that advice.
sources.quote: helping search engines understand your content

sources.claim: Opening and tool choice: Search Console monitors Google Search presence; it is free and registration is not needed for inclusion.
sources.quote: You don't have to sign up for Search Console to be included in Google Search results

sources.claim: Tool choice and monthly checklist: URL Inspection reports individual-page index status; sitemap submission is optional; check around monthly or after changes; email alerts cover newly found issues.
sources.quote: check your account around once every month, or when you make changes to the site's content

sources.claim: Connect Search Console: add and verify a property or obtain existing-owner access. Domain coverage includes subdomains and protocols; DNS verification applies to independently hosted Domain properties. Exact URL-prefix coverage includes protocol and subdomain. Examples apply the documented matching rules.
sources.quote: Includes only URLs with the specified prefix, including the protocol (http/https).

sources.claim: Indexing section and tip: indexed pages are eligible for results; use URL Inspection for individual pages, investigate reasons, and expect some legitimate exclusions. Indexing does not ensure appearance or a fixed rank.
sources.quote: Just because a page is indexed doesn't guarantee that it will show up in your search results.

sources.claim: Content section and review checklist: distinct concise descriptive page titles; avoid vague Home labels and boilerplate. The Grace Church title is an original illustrative application.
sources.quote: Write descriptive and concise text for your <title> elements.

sources.claim: Content section and checklist: write page-specific descriptions; Google primarily generates snippets from page content and sometimes chooses the meta description. CMS settings may expose the description field.
sources.quote: Snippets are primarily created from the page content itself.

sources.claim: Analytics introduction: GA4 uses event-based website and app data; setup is optional guidance for readers choosing this tool.
sources.quote: Uses event-based data instead of session-based

sources.claim: Analytics setup checklist: account and property, time zone, Web stream, optional enhanced measurement, supported CMS tag ID field or other tag installation, Realtime verification. Important callout identifies the first-party setup guidance to reconfirm.
sources.quote: creating a Google Analytics property, adding a data stream, and adding your Google Analytics code.

sources.claim: Troubleshooting paragraph: verify account/property and matching tag ID and installation on relevant pages; using direct tag and Tag Manager implementations together can overcount.
sources.quote: Using both methods will have unintended consequences, such as overcounting data from your website.

sources.claim: Metrics section and review checklist: Search Console impressions, clicks, CTR calculation, Queries and Pages views and date range selection.
sources.quote: CTR (click-through rate): The click count divided by the impression count.

sources.claim: Tool table, metrics section and review checklist: Traffic acquisition includes new and returning users, session traffic sources and channel groups; Editors and above can restore a missing report.
sources.quote: It specifically shows where new and returning users come from.

sources.claim: Metrics section: a session measures a period of interaction, a user can have several sessions, and session counts are estimates; therefore retain the sessions label rather than treating it as a count of people.
sources.quote: A session is a period of time during which a user interacts with your website or app.

sources.claim: Tool table, metrics section and review checklist: events measure specific interactions or occurrences; mark a meaningful action as a key event and verify event names/parameters in Realtime or DebugView.
sources.quote: measure a specific interaction or occurrence

sources.claim: Privacy section, warning and final checklist: Google prohibits recognizable PII including email/mobile data. Check automatically collected URLs/titles, query parameters, user search/form input and custom event data; avoid personal form responses in analytics.
sources.quote: Both the URL path and parameters must be free of PII.

sources.claim: Privacy section: Analytics use and data processing must be disclosed under Google policy; compare the actual setup to the notice before enabling.
sources.quote: you must disclose the use of Google Analytics and how it collects and processes data.

sources.claim: Privacy section: review available Analytics account data-sharing settings.
sources.quote: There are several data sharing settings in your Analytics account.

sources.claim: Scripture callout: exact Proverbs 18:13 LSB, checked individually at the official reading site. Line break normalized to a space; no interpretive claim added.
sources.publisher: The Lockman Foundation / Three Sixteen Publishing
sources.quote: He who responds with a word before he hears, It is folly and shame to him.

sources.quote: keyword stuffing is against Google's spam policies

sources.claim: Content section: Google does not set a ranking word-count target.
sources.quote: there's no magical word count target

sources.claim: Tool choice: Search Console is free.
sources.quote: free service

sources.claim: Tool choice: adding a Search Console property only enables tracking rather than improving search position.
sources.quote: Adding a property does not affect your website

sources.claim: Analytics setup: compare Measurement ID to the installed tag ID.
sources.quote: The Google tag ID is incorrect

sources.claim: Metrics definitions: Search Console impressions measure appearances.
sources.quote: How many times your site appeared in Search results.

sources.claim: Traffic acquisition section: Editors and Administrators can restore the report.
sources.quote: Editors (and above) can add it back to the left navigation.

sources.claim: Metrics section: Analytics session counts are estimated.
sources.quote: by estimating the number of unique session IDs.

sources.claim: Events section: event parameters can be verified in DebugView.
sources.quote: verify that you have set up an event and event parameters correctly.

sources.claim: Privacy section: Google policy identifies email addresses and personal mobile numbers as PII.
sources.quote: email addresses, personal mobile numbers

sources.claim: Privacy section: the basic page tag collects addresses and page titles.
sources.quote: page URL and page title

sources.claim: Verification section: DNS verification uses a record at the domain provider; ask the domain/website manager to follow the relevant platform instructions.
sources.quote: Add a DNS record to your domain provider's record list to prove ownership.

sources.claim: Content section and opening: use descriptive links relevant to the linked page.
sources.quote: Good anchor text is descriptive, reasonably concise, and relevant to the page that it's on and to the page it links to.

sources.claim: Indexing section: a sitemap describes important pages/files; a CMS may already supply it. Provider consultation is the article's practical application.
sources.quote: A sitemap tells search engines which pages and files you think are important in your site

sources.claim: Opening and content section: create helpful material for intended visitors rather than manipulating rankings. The church-specific examples apply this principle.
sources.quote: helpful, reliable information that's created to benefit people

Resolved 2026-10-16: use three nearest published website/privacy/listings articles as related reading; do not repeat map-listing procedures or change their privacy guidance.
Resolved 2026-10-16: Analytics is optional; no advertising, retargeting, personal-data imports, attendance targets or legal thresholds are prescribed.

Resolved 2026-10-16: Google sources are tagged vendor because they document their own services; they are first-party evidence. The official LSB verse is tagged primary. All source access dates and platform guidance are as of 2026-10-16.
